title: Structural basis of the gating mechanism of the large-conductance mechanosensitive channel from Escherichia coli
task: Elucidate structural mechanism of MscL gating
key_results: Solved closed-state structures (DMPC, DOPC nanodiscs) and expanded-state structure by cryo-EM; PELDOR/DEER shows conformational ensemble shifts in DSPC; identified closed-to-expanded transition dynamics via H/D-MS and MD
comments: Integration of multiple structural and biophysical techniques is thorough, but the physiological lipid composition relevance to bacterial mechanosensing could be further explored.

model_io.model: EcMscL in lipid nanodiscs (DMPC, DOPC, DSPC)
Molecular dynamics simulations of EcMscL gating
outputs: Dynamics of residues in closed-to-expanded transition

hypotheses.hypothesis: High-resolution structures reveal precise gating mechanism
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; expanded-state architecture consistent with prior electrophysiology; transition sites identified

title: The SIMDA framework maps PIP2-binding sites regulating the KCNQ1 channel
task: Map PIP2-binding sites and dynamics on KCNQ1 channel
key_results: SIMDA framework identified six recurrent PIP2 sites (C0-C5) across 2000 µs simulations; C1 and C3 match experimental densities; KCNE3 stabilizes C1 via C-terminal twist; CaM modulates C4/C5; dynamic circular transfer pathways revealed
comments: The multi-scale MD approach is sophisticated and forward predictions are testable, but functional validation of predicted sites C0, C4, C5 by electrophysiology would strengthen claims.

model_io.model: KCNQ1 channel with KCNE3, CaM, and PIP2 in eight functional states

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multiple recurrent PIP2-binding sites regulate KCNQ1 through state-dependent mechanisms
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; six sites identified with state-dependent populations; KCNE3 and CaM modulate distinct sites

title: An additional water is introduced into the manganese cluster during the formation of the S3 state of photosystem II
task: Determine whether water insertion occurs in Mn4Ca cluster during S3 state formation in PSII
key_results: High-resolution data (~1.9 Å) for S1, S2, S3 states with anomalous diffraction confirm new oxygen OX (O6) ligand in S3 state; OX-O5 distance ~2.1 Å indicates no strong interaction in S3, suggesting O-O bond forms in S3→S0 transition
comments: High-resolution crystallography with anomalous data provides strong evidence for the water insertion, though temporal resolution of the S3→S0 bond-formation step remains challenging.

model_io.model: Photosystem II Mn4Ca cluster in S1, S2, S3 states
inputs: X-ray photons at 9.5 keV and 7 keV (anomalous)

hypotheses.hypothesis: New oxygen ligand inserts into Mn4Ca cluster during S3 formation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; OX observable as distinct peak; ligated to Mn1 and Ca

hypotheses.hypothesis: O-O bond forms in S3 state
hypotheses.result: Not supported; OX-O5 distance 2.1 Å indicates weak/absent interaction; likely bond formation occurs in S3→S0

title: Mapping of dynamic allostery within p38 alpha kinase via network analyses and NMR spectroscopy
task: Map allosteric communication pathways in p38α kinase
key_results: Identified dynamic allostery between N- and C-lobes involving allosteric site, activation loop, and cryptic lipid-binding pocket; validated via NMR and activity assays on wildtype and mutants
comments: Network analysis combined with experimental validation provides mechanistic insight but the clinical translation to selective allosteric inhibitor design remains to be demonstrated.

model_io.model: p38α kinase (wildtype and mutants)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dynamic allostery connects N- and C-lobes through specific residue networks
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; pathways involve allosteric site, activation loop, and C-lobe cryptic pocket

title: Extracellular-matrix mediated stresses spatially bias myoblast fusion and myotube growth
task: Determine how ECM-mediated stresses regulate myoblast fusion and myotube growth
key_results: Myoblasts form active nematic system; fusion events preferentially accumulate near +1/2 topological defects with high compressive stress; ECM remodeling stabilizes defects; fusion-driven growth increases nematic order and stress magnitude
comments: The coupling of cell nematic order, ECM remodeling, and fusion location is elegant and experimentally validated, but quantitative prediction of fusion efficiency from stress patterns requires further development.

model_io.model: Primary myoblasts cultured on ECM
Theoretical nematic model of myoblast system

hypotheses.hypothesis: ECM-stabilized nematic stress patterns spatially bias fusion localization
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; fusion accumulates near +1/2 defects with high compressive stress predicted by theory

title: Complete strategy spaces reveal hidden pathways to cooperation
task: Determine if complete strategy spaces alter evolutionary cooperation outcomes
key_results: Full eight-strategy deterministic space reveals cooperation sustained via cyclic dynamics (suspicious cooperation) absent in restricted models; stable coexistence of up to seven strategies observed
comments: The analytical and simulation results convincingly show model completeness matters, though biological relevance depends on whether real agents can execute all eight strategies.

model_io.model: Two-stage cheap-talk game with complete deterministic strategies

hypotheses.hypothesis: Restricted strategy sets misrepresent cooperation evolution
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; complete space reveals hidden cyclic pathways and wider cooperation parameter regions

title: Succinate exacerbates obesity-associated osteoarthritis: mitochondrial dysfunction mediated by SUCNR1 activation and succinylation modification
task: Decipher succinate-driven mitochondrial dysfunction in obesity-associated osteoarthritis
key_results: Succinate accumulates in OA joints; exacerbates cartilage degeneration via SUCNR1-mediated mitochondrial fission and mtROS accumulation through IDH2 succinylation; SIRT5 acts as protective desuccinylase
comments: Integrates metabolic signaling with post-translational modifications to explain obesity-OA link; therapeutic hydrogel targets both extracellular and intracellular pools.

model_io.model: High-fat diet mouse OA model + chondrocytes

hypotheses.hypothesis: Extracellular succinate via SUCNR1 triggers mitochondrial fission and cGAS-STING activation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; mitochondrial fission and STING pathway activation observed

hypotheses.hypothesis: SIRT5 desuccinylase activity protects against succinate-induced degeneration
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; SIRT5 agonist puerarin reduces cartilage damage in vivo

title: XPO1-mediated TRIM21 nuclear export reprograms TREM2+ macrophage polarization by targeting IRF3 to augment anti-PD-1 efficacy in small cell lung cancer

title: Differential lipid selectivity of StARD phospholipid transporters revealed by native MS
task: Determine lipid selectivity mechanisms and regulation of StARD phospholipid transporter family
key_results: STARD7 exhibits broad phospholipid binding; STARD2 prefers polyunsaturated lipids; STARD10 prefers diunsaturated lipids; conserved arginine essential for STARD7 but dispensable for others; phosphorylation in membrane-binding regions abolishes STARD10 transfer activity
comments: Native MS approach elegantly reveals endogenous lipid ligands and selectivity architecture; phosphorylation as regulatory switch provides mechanistic insight into activity control.

model_io.model: Purified recombinant STARD2/7/10 + native MS; liposome transfer assays

hypotheses.hypothesis: StARD transporters exhibit distinct lipid selectivities linked to acyl chain properties
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; STARD7 broad-spectrum, STARD2 polyunsaturated-selective, STARD10 diunsaturated-selective

hypotheses.hypothesis: Phosphorylation regulates LTP activity and lipid selectivity
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; phosphorylation abolishes STARD10 transfer activity

title: A somatic checkpoint through NHR-49/HNF4α governs reproductive investment and longevity in C. elegans
task: Characterize NHR-49/HNF4α-mediated reproductive-metabolic checkpoint governing fertility and longevity
key_results: NHR-49 loss causes inappropriate oocyte activation and yolk depletion, drastically shortening lifespan; NHR-49 acts somatically to regulate oocyte biology; NHR-49 couples germline proliferation to starvation response via GSA-1/Gαs transcriptional control
comments: Reveals nutrient-sensing mechanism linking reproductive investment to organismal longevity; somatic control of germline function is mechanistically surprising.

hypotheses.hypothesis: GSA-1/Gαs is direct NHR-49 transcriptional target linking metabolic sensing to fertility

title: Deletion of P311 enhances regeneration in aged skeletal muscle
task: Determine P311's role in age-dependent fibrosis suppression and skeletal muscle regeneration capacity
key_results: P311 expression increases with age and injury; P311 knockout in aged muscle reduces TGF-β production and fibrosis, enhances fiber regrowth and force recovery; P311 deletion in FAPs reduces fibrogenic capacity
comments: Identifies P311 as aging-associated fibrosis driver; single-cell RNA-seq localizes P311 expression to fibroblast/FAP populations, providing cellular context for therapeutic targeting.

model_io.model: Young (4-7mo) and old (24mo) wild-type and P311−/− mice + BaCl2 muscle injury

hypotheses.hypothesis: P311 loss reduces age-associated fibrosis and improves regeneration

hypotheses.hypothesis: P311 in FAPs is sufficient to drive fibrogenesis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; FAP-specific P311 deletion reduces fibrogenic capacity

title: An epithelial-derived epigenetic clock reveals pathway-level aging mechanisms in chronic lung disease
task: Develop tissue-specific epigenetic clocks revealing pathway-level aging mechanisms in lung disease
key_results: PathwayAge epithelial clock (MAE=2.86, Rho=0.97) identifies ABL1/SOX9/MEF2C pathway dysregulation as epithelial aging hallmark; parenchymal clock (MAE=4.36-4.60, Rho=0.889-0.899) reveals SOX4/WNT3A/LRRK2-driven pro-inflammatory transition; age acceleration correlates with smoking burden and disease severity
comments: Superior mechanistic interpretability vs. conventional epigenetic clocks through pathway-level projection; identifies convergent disease mechanisms (epithelial regeneration loss, inflammation, ECM remodeling).

model_io.model: Human airway epithelium and lung parenchyma; DNA methylation profiling

hypotheses.hypothesis: Tissue-specific pathway-level projection improves epigenetic clock accuracy and interpretability
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; PathwayAge clocks achieve high correlation with chronological age across independent cohorts

hypotheses.hypothesis: Distinct aging architectures characterize epithelium vs. parenchyma
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; epithelial aging driven by adhesion pathway dysregulation; parenchymal by developmental/metabolic rewiring

title: Alanine tRNA fragments interacting with MEG3 long splice variant show tissue-, cellular compartment- and disease severity-dependent changes in Parkinson’s disease
task: Characterize alanine tRNA fragment-lncRNA interactions in Parkinson's disease pathophysiology
key_results: MEG3 long splice variant interacts with 3'-tRFs-Ala; both dysregulated in PD substantia nigra; PD-risk carriers (LRRK2+, GBA+, SNCA+) show decreased blood 3'-tRFs-Ala; GBA+ patients show correlation between reduced 3'-tRFs-Ala and autonomic/sensory impairment severity

hypotheses.hypothesis: Oxidative stress redistributes 3'-tRFs-Ala from nucleus to cytoplasm

title: A Network pharmacology and experimental study of dihydroartemisinin in drug-resistant non-small cell lung cancer involving AURKA modulation

key_results: DHA inhibits A549/DDP proliferation (IC50 23.18 μM at 72h); induces both apoptosis (BAX↑/BCL-2↓) and ferroptosis (ROS↑, GPX4↓); synergizes with AURKA inhibitor VX-680 via AURKA/GSK3β/NRF2 axis

task: Elucidate PER2-KRAS physical interaction and PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway attenuation in glioma suppression

title: SHP2 accelerated acute liver injury via modulating TGFβ1/EZH2/BRD4 signaling induced proliferation and fibrosis of HSC

title: Paeoniflorin inhibited macrophage polarization via glycolysis pathway to protect against sepsis-induced intestinal injury
task: Elucidate paeoniflorin's protective mechanism in sepsis-induced intestinal injury via macrophage glycolysis inhibition
key_results: Paeoniflorin increases CLP sepsis survival dose-dependently; decreases M1 markers and glycolytic enzyme HK2/PKM2/LDHA; induces M2 polarization and restores intestinal tight junction (ZO-1, occludin); PKM2 activator TEPP-46 reverses all protective effects
comments: Demonstrates M1/M2 balance as glycolysis-dependent process; mechanistic validation via PKM2 modulation is elegant and highlights metabolic rewiring as polarization driver.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Macrophage M1→M2 shift restores intestinal barrier function and reduces systemic inflammation

title: Impaired protein translation inhibits DNA replication by a Claspin-Chk1-Rif1 pathway

key_results: Protein synthesis inhibition rapidly suppresses DNA synthesis via Claspin-Chk1-Rif1 pathway without detectable DNA damage; CK1-alpha and Cdc7 phosphorylate Claspin to transmit signal

title: Transient CB2R modulation durably restricts breast cancer plasticity by stabilizing a luminal like cell identity

title: Intensity–complexity post-triage prioritization to shorten waiting times in emergency departments
